note: Sizes measured by tools/report-sizes.mjs from a real `vite build`. After the redesign only five libraries are on the main page; the rest are demonstrated on /lab.html. Keeping five out is the result, not an omission.

libraries.name: GSAP + ScrollTrigger
libraries.role: Scroll orchestration: the pinned hero flight, the scrubbed copy exit, and ScrollTrigger.refresh() management.
libraries.why: Anthropic's own launch pages ship GSAP + ScrollTrigger for exactly this (confirmed by finding it in their dynamically-imported chunks). One pinned scroll-scrub plus a handful of triggers; no more.

libraries.name: Lenis
libraries.role: Inertial smooth scrolling, driven by the GSAP ticker so both share one rAF loop.
libraries.why: The reference sites do not use smooth scrolling at all — and that was worth learning. Kept because the flight camera reads better against interpolated scroll, but it is the first thing I would cut if it ever fought the native feel.

libraries.name: SplitType
libraries.role: Demonstrated on the lab page; no longer used on the main page.
libraries.why: Anthropic's hero resolves with a 26px blur-in, not a per-word split reveal. I built the split version first, compared them, and the blur-in won — so SplitType came out of the critical path rather than being kept because it was already integrated.

libraries.name: three.js
libraries.role: Demonstrated on the lab page; the main page no longer loads it.
libraries.why: It powered two heroes here — first a shader aurora, then an instanced agent graph with a bloom/DOF/halation chain. Both were replaced by a canvas Context Window, because the brief moved from 'look at this render' to 'read this idea', and text does not need a GPU. At 138.5 KB gzip it was also the single largest thing on the page. Still the best tool in the set for real 3D, and still demonstrated on the lab page.

libraries.name: Motion (motion.dev)
libraries.role: Demonstrated on the lab page; no longer used on the main page.
libraries.why: The reference design language is cubic-bezier(.165,.84,.44,1) transitions and hover = opacity .85. Springs were the wrong physics for it. Kept in the lab because it is genuinely the best tool for retargetable UI springs.

libraries.name: anime.js
libraries.role: Demonstrated on the lab page; the diagram it drove was removed from the portfolio.
libraries.why: The best tool of the ten for pure SVG choreography — DrawSVG and MotionPath equivalents are built in rather than plugins. It was carrying the agent-architecture diagram, which has been cut from the portfolio, so anime.js is now only demonstrable here.

libraries.name: tsParticles (hand-composed)
libraries.role: Demonstrated on the lab page; superseded on the main page by the WebGL scene.
libraries.why: The old design used it for a contact-card particle field. The 3D chapter now owns particles, and running both would be two systems doing one job.

libraries.name: Lottie (lottie_light)
libraries.role: Demonstrated on the lab page with the bespoke agent-core animation and a third-party chart.
libraries.why: The bespoke asset is generated for this project and license-clean, but it lived in the old hero profile card, which the 3D chapter replaced. The runtime and asset remain in the lab.

libraries.name: Rive (@rive-app/canvas)
libraries.role: Demonstrated on the lab page with the MIT-licensed rating.riv.
libraries.why: Runtime is MIT and excellent; .riv can only be authored in the Rive editor and exporting needs a paid plan, so no on-brand asset exists to ship.

libraries.name: AutoAnimate
libraries.role: FLIP reflow of the capability grid when the filter chips change what is rendered.
libraries.why: The only place the DOM genuinely changes shape at runtime, and 3 KB to solve it properly.
